correctness.rationale: At P=pi/2 and a=(kappa-kappa^{-1})/2, direct conjugated-rotation line geometry gives acute principal-angle increment g_kappa(theta)=P-arctan(a|sin(2theta)|), with period P and Lipschitz constant 2a. The lift of arg(B_kappa e_theta) has derivative (kappa cos²theta+kappa^{-1}sin²theta)^{-1} <= kappa. Replacing one actual step P+t/N by P costs <= kappa|t|/N; the left Riemann sum for g(theta+tu) costs <=a|t|/N, proving the uniform (kappa+a)|t|/N and Hausdorff bounds for every N and real t. Circular unimodality places residual-window extrema at centers 0 and P/2 and yields W=(2/|t|)integral_0^{r/2}[atan(a cos2u)-atan(a sin2u)]du, r=|t| mod P; width vanishes exactly for nonzero integral quarter turns, with nonzero linear-cusp coefficient atan(a)/(|m|P). Full-period cancellation and the same uniform estimate establish the three detuning regimes for delta_N->0. Independent numerical evaluation of both principal-angle formulas and sliding-window width for kappa=1.3,2,4.5 and eight detunings, with 1001 phase samples, corroborated the formulas; the all-N/all-real proof is analytic.
